tool_input.command:
# Get initial size
$gitDir = ".git"
$initialSize = (Get-ChildItem -Path $gitDir -Recurse -Force | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1MB
Write-Host "Initial .git size: $($initialSize)MB"

# Run aggressive garbage collection and cleanup
Write-Host "Running git gc..."
git gc --aggressive --prune=now

# Get final size
$finalSize = (Get-ChildItem -Path $gitDir -Recurse -Force | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1MB
$reclaimed = $initialSize - $finalSize
Write-Host "Final .git size: $($finalSize)MB"
Write-Host "Space reclaimed: $($reclaimed)MB"
tool_input.description: Measure git directory size before and after running aggressive garbage collection

tool_input.command:
# Get initial size
$gitDir = ".git"
$initialSize = (Get-ChildItem -Path $gitDir -Recurse -Force | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1MB
Write-Host "Initial .git size: $($initialSize)MB"

# Run garbage collection (safer version)
Write-Host "Running git gc --aggressive..."
git gc --aggressive

# Also clean up reflog
Write-Host "Expiring reflog entries..."
git reflog expire --all --expire=now

# Get final size
$finalSize = (Get-ChildItem -Path $gitDir -Recurse -Force | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum / 1MB
$reclaimed = $initialSize - $finalSize
Write-Host "Final .git size: $($finalSize)MB"
Write-Host "Space reclaimed: $($reclaimed)MB"
tool_input.description: Run git garbage collection and expire reflog without immediate pruning

result:
Done. Git's aggressive garbage collection repacked the repository objects efficiently, reclaiming **0.036 MB** (~36 KB). The `.git` directory is now **0.230 MB** (down from 0.266 MB).

For a checkout this size, the savings are modest. Larger repositories with more history typically see more significant space recovery from this operation.
